claim: Experience-dependent cortical plasticity is a pivotal process of human brain development and essential for the formation of most cognitive functions.
source: Experience-dependent cortical plasticity is a pivotal process of human brain development and essential for the formation of most cognitive functions.
evidence: This is a general statement about the importance of experience-dependent plasticity, drawing from established scientific understanding.

claim: Early visual experience could influence the endogenous development of visual cortex in animals.
source: Although studies found that early visual experience could influence the endogenous development of visual cortex in animals, little is known about such impact on human infants.
evidence: This claim references previous studies on animals, indicating it is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Little is known about the impact of early visual experience on the endogenous development of visual cortex in human infants.
source: Although studies found that early visual experience could influence the endogenous development of visual cortex in animals, little is known about such impact on human infants.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge, based on the authors' assessment of the literature.

claim: Postnatal time selectively modulated the cortical thickness in the ventral visual cortex.
source: Particularly, we found that postnatal time selectively modulated the cortical thickness in the ventral visual cortex and the functional circuit between bilateral primary visual cortices.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: Postnatal time modulated the functional circuit between bilateral primary visual cortices.
source: Particularly, we found that postnatal time selectively modulated the cortical thickness in the ventral visual cortex and the functional circuit between bilateral primary visual cortices.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: Cortical myelination developed without significant influence of postnatal time in the early neonatal period.
source: But the cortical myelination and functional connections of the high-order visual cortex developed without significant influence of postnatal time in such an early period.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: Functional connections of the high-order visual cortex developed without significant influence of postnatal time in the early neonatal period.
source: But the cortical myelination and functional connections of the high-order visual cortex developed without significant influence of postnatal time in such an early period.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: Postnatal time had a direct influence on the development of homotopic connection in area V1.
source: The structure–function analysis further revealed that the postnatal time had a direct influence on the development of homotopic connection in area V1, while gestational time had an indirect effect on it through cortical myelination.
evidence: This is a finding from the mediation analysis performed in the study.

claim: Gestational time had an indirect effect on the development of homotopic connection in area V1 through cortical myelination.
source: The structure–function analysis further revealed that the postnatal time had a direct influence on the development of homotopic connection in area V1, while gestational time had an indirect effect on it through cortical myelination.
evidence: This is a finding from the mediation analysis performed in the study.

claim: The findings were validated in preterm-born infants who had longer postnatal time but shorter gestational time at birth.
source: These findings were further validated in preterm-born infants who had longer postnatal time but shorter gestational time at birth.
evidence: This describes a validation analysis performed in the study comparing term and preterm infants.

claim: Early postnatal time shaped the structural and functional development of the visual cortex in selective and organized patterns in human newborns.
source: In short, these data suggested in human newborns that early postnatal time shaped the structural and functional development of the visual cortex in selective and organized patterns.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the study's data.

claim: A framework consisting of two distinct phases was proposed to describe the development of visual cortex.
source: Vision, given its ecological universality and importance across species, has long been taken as a representative modality to investigate such question (Barlow, 1975; Crair et al., 1998; Gödecke and Bonhoeffer, 1996; Li et al., 2008; Li et al., 2006; Roy et al., 2020), and a framework consisting of two distinct phases was proposed to describe the development of visual cortex (Barlow, 1975; Li et al., 2006; White and Fitzpatrick, 2007).
evidence: This references a theoretical framework from prior literature.

claim: The framework includes an early, experience-independent phase in which the basic layout of neural map is established.
source: This framework includes an early, experience-independent phase in which the basic layout of neural map is established, and a subsequently experience-dependent phase in which the visual experience refines and shapes the initial neural map.
evidence: This describes a theoretical framework from prior literature.

claim: The framework includes a subsequently experience-dependent phase in which the visual experience refines and shapes the initial neural map.
source: This framework includes an early, experience-independent phase in which the basic layout of neural map is established, and a subsequently experience-dependent phase in which the visual experience refines and shapes the initial neural map.
evidence: This describes a theoretical framework from prior literature.

claim: Recent studies revealed the importance of visual experience during the early period of cortical development.
source: Recent studies further revealed the importance of visual experience during the early period of cortical development, suggesting the intricate interaction between early sensory experience and the endogenous mechanisms in neurodevelopment (Li et al., 2008; Li et al., 2006; Roy et al., 2020).
evidence: This references findings from recent studies in the literature.

claim: There is an intricate interaction between early sensory experience and the endogenous mechanisms in neurodevelopment.
source: Recent studies further revealed the importance of visual experience during the early period of cortical development, suggesting the intricate interaction between early sensory experience and the endogenous mechanisms in neurodevelopment (Li et al., 2008; Li et al., 2006; Roy et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an interpretation of findings from cited studies.

claim: Studies on the importance of visual experience during early cortical development were carried out on model animals using electrophysiological techniques.
source: However, these studies were carried out on the model animals (e.g., cat and ferret) using electrophysiological techniques.
evidence: This describes the methodology of previous studies.

claim: The influence of early postnatal experience on the development of visual cortex in human infants remains unclear.
source: Due to the lack of noninvasive methods to probe the human infant brain, the influence of early postnatal experience on the development of visual cortex in human infants remains unclear.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge based on methodological limitations.

claim: MRI provided an ideal tool to noninvasively measure both the brain structure and function.
source: Neuroimaging techniques, especially magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), provided an ideal tool to noninvasively measure both the brain structure and function, which, however, remains challenging for the infants' brain due to subject motion, limited resolution, and difficulty in patient recruitment (Cordero-Grande et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a general statement about MRI capabilities, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: MRI of infants' brain remains challenging due to subject motion, limited resolution, and difficulty in patient recruitment.
source: Neuroimaging techniques, especially magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), provided an ideal tool to noninvasively measure both the brain structure and function, which, however, remains challenging for the infants' brain due to subject motion, limited resolution, and difficulty in patient recruitment (Cordero-Grande et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes known challenges in infant MRI, supported by citation.

claim: The developing human connectome project was initiated to investigate the early structural and functional development of human cerebral cortex.
source: Owing to the recent technical advances in both images acquisition and processing methods (Hughes et al., 2017), MRI studies of the perinatal brain, for example, the developing human connectome project (dHCP; http://www.developingconnectome.org/) was initiated to investigate the early structural and functional development of human cerebral cortex.
evidence: This describes the purpose of the dHCP project.

claim: The study collected a dataset of multimodal MRI data of 407 neonatal subjects from dHCP.
source: Herein we collected a dataset of multimodal MRI data of 407 neonatal subjects from dHCP to address the above question.
evidence: This describes the dataset used in the study.

claim: The different time intervals between gestational age at birth and the postmenstrual age at scan indicated the difference in the postnatal experience across neonates.
source: The different time intervals between gestational age (GA) at birth and the postmenstrual age (PMA) at scan indicated the difference in the postnatal experience across neonates, which reflects the individual variation of the visual experience.
evidence: This is a logical inference about what the time intervals represent.

claim: The time window between GA at birth and PMA at scan provides the opportunity to investigate the contributions of early visual experience versus endogenous neurodevelopment on the development of visual cortex in human newborns.
source: Thus, this time window provides us the opportunity to investigate the contributions of early visual experience versus endogenous neurodevelopment on the development of visual cortex in human newborns.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the research opportunity provided by the data.

claim: The VOTC contains function-specific regions for biologically important categories such as faces, bodies, and scenes.
source: The VOTC contains function-specific regions for biologically important categories such as faces (Kanwisher et al., 1998), bodies (Downing et al., 2001), and scenes (Epstein and Kanwisher, 1998), making this region a critical component in the ventral pathway of visual processing (Bi et al., 2016; Grill-Spector and Malach, 2004; Grill-Spector and Weiner, 2014; Kanwisher, 2010), and the impact of early visual experience on those regions is not fully understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research on VOTC function.

claim: The VOTC is a critical component in the ventral pathway of visual processing.
source: The VOTC contains function-specific regions for biologically important categories such as faces (Kanwisher et al., 1998), bodies (Downing et al., 2001), and scenes (Epstein and Kanwisher, 1998), making this region a critical component in the ventral pathway of visual processing (Bi et al., 2016; Grill-Spector and Malach, 2004; Grill-Spector and Weiner, 2014; Kanwisher, 2010), and the impact of early visual experience on those regions is not fully understood.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The impact of early visual experience on VOTC regions is not fully understood.
source: The VOTC contains function-specific regions for biologically important categories such as faces (Kanwisher et al., 1998), bodies (Downing et al., 2001), and scenes (Epstein and Kanwisher, 1998), making this region a critical component in the ventral pathway of visual processing (Bi et al., 2016; Grill-Spector and Malach, 2004; Grill-Spector and Weiner, 2014; Kanwisher, 2010), and the impact of early visual experience on those regions is not fully understood.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: Previous studies described the developmental trajectory of CT and CM in human infants and found a generally increasing trend for both measurements with PMA in whole brain.
source: Previous studies have described the developmental trajectory of CT and CM in human infants and found a generally increasing trend for both two measurements with PMA in whole brain (Bozek et al., 2018; Fenchel et al., 2020).
evidence: This references findings from prior studies.

claim: The contribution of PT to the development of CT and CM was not clarified in previous studies because PMA reflects both prenatal and postnatal factors.
source: But the contribution of PT to the development was not clarified because PMA reflects both prenatal and postnatal factors.
evidence: This identifies a limitation in previous research.

claim: Primate newborns at a few days of age already had a proto-organization in visual system.
source: Using r-fMRI, studies found that the primate newborns at a few days of age already had a proto-organization in visual system (Arcaro and Livingstone, 2017) and human infants within a few weeks of age showed a category-specific network (Kamps et al., 2020).
evidence: This references findings from a prior study.

claim: Human infants within a few weeks of age showed a category-specific network.
source: Using r-fMRI, studies found that the primate newborns at a few days of age already had a proto-organization in visual system (Arcaro and Livingstone, 2017) and human infants within a few weeks of age showed a category-specific network (Kamps et al., 2020).
evidence: This references findings from a prior study.

claim: The small sample size of previous r-fMRI studies might undermine reliability of the results given the well-known instability of r-fMRI signals.
source: However, the small sample size of those studies might undermine reliability of the results given the well-known instability of r-fMRI signals (Poldrack et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a critical assessment of prior studies, supported by citation about r-fMRI instability.

claim: Human infants in a previous study were around 1 month old (mean age: 27 days; range from 6 to 57 days).
source: Moreover, the human infants participating in a previous study (Kamps et al., 2020) were around 1 month old (mean age: 27 days; range from 6 to 57 days), who might already acquire some visual experience, and thus this study could not exclude postnatal visual experience on the innate functional connectivity.
evidence: This describes the sample characteristics of a prior study.

claim: A previous study could not exclude postnatal visual experience on the innate functional connectivity because infants might already acquire some visual experience.
source: Moreover, the human infants participating in a previous study (Kamps et al., 2020) were around 1 month old (mean age: 27 days; range from 6 to 57 days), who might already acquire some visual experience, and thus this study could not exclude postnatal visual experience on the innate functional connectivity.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of a limitation in a prior study.

claim: The study included 407 neonates (187 females, PMA = 41.11 ± 1.73 weeks at scan).
source: To show the general developmental trajectories of CT and CM in the visual cortex during the human neonatal period, we included 407 neonates (187 females, PMA = 41.11 ± 1.73 weeks at scan) from a total dataset of 783 subjects after excluding data that did not pass quality control or did not satisfy inclusion criteria ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This describes the study sample.

claim: 355 of the neonates were term-born (PMA = 41.14 ± 1.70, range from 37.43 to 44.71 weeks at scan).
source: In total, 355 of them were term-born (PMA = 41.14 ± 1.70, range from 37.43 to 44.71 weeks at scan; Figure 1a).
evidence: This describes the study sample.

claim: The CT and CM of the ventral cortex significantly increased between 37 and 45 weeks of PMA (r = 0.40–0.49, p<10–9).
source: In general, the CT and CM of the ventral cortex significantly increased between 37 and 45 weeks of PMA (r = 0.40–0.49, p<10–9; Figure 1b–d).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Both CT and CM showed higher correlation with PMA in the posterior than anterior region (r = –0.8 and –0.83; p<0.001).
source: Generally, both CT and CM showed higher correlation with PMA in the posterior than anterior region (r = –0.8 and –0.83; p<0.001), and higher correlation in the medial than lateral part within the ventral visual cortex (r = 0.7 and 0.91; p<0.001; Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Both CT and CM showed higher correlation with PMA in the medial than lateral part within the ventral visual cortex (r = 0.7 and 0.91; p<0.001).

claim: The GA of the study population was 39.93 ± 1.26 weeks.
source: The GA of our study population was 39.93 ± 1.26 weeks and the PT was 1.21 ± 1.25 weeks, and the correlation between them was not significant (r = –0.08, p>0.1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

claim: The PT of the study population was 1.21 ± 1.25 weeks.

claim: The correlation between GA and PT was not significant (r = –0.08, p>0.1).

claim: GA was significantly related to the CM (r = 0.53 and 0.51 for right and left hemisphere, respectively; p<10–9).
source: The results showed that the GA was significantly related to the CM (r = 0.53 and 0.51 for right and left hemisphere, respectively; p<10–9) and CT (r = 0.16 and 0.14; p<0.05) averaged in the whole ventral mask.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: GA was significantly related to the CT (r = 0.16 and 0.14; p<0.05) averaged in the whole ventral mask.

claim: CM was significantly correlated with GA in all 68 ROIs (r > 0.28, FDR-corrected q < 0.05).
source: In terms of regional correlation, the CM was significantly correlated with GA in all 68 ROIs (r > 0.28, false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected q < 0.05), while CT showed significant correlation only in 23 ROIs (r > 0.13, FDR-corrected q < 0.05) (Figure 2a and b).

source: The PT was significantly correlated with CT (r = 0.53 and 0.51 for left and right ventral cortex, p<10–9) for left and right ventral cortex, with 61 of the 68 ROIs showing significant positive correlation (all r > 0.11, FDR-corrected q < 0.05).

claim: Only two ROIs in the anterior temporal areas showed significant effects of PT on CM.

evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: GA had a significantly stronger effect on the CM than PT (interaction between GA and PT, p<0.05).
source: We applied a linear mixed-effect model to test whether the CT (or CM) of the whole ventral cortex was differently influenced by the GA versus PT and found that the GA had a significantly stronger effect on the CM than PT (interaction between GA and PT, p<0.05) but no significant difference was found on the development of CT (p>0.6).

claim: No significant difference was found between GA and PT on the development of CT (p>0.6).
source: We applied a linear mixed-effect model to test whether the CT (or CM) of the whole ventral cortex was differently influenced by the GA versus PT and found that the GA had a significantly stronger effect on the CM than PT (interaction between GA and PT, p<0.05) but no significant difference was found on the development of CT (p>0.6).

source: Taken together, those results suggested that the development of CM heavily depends on the endogenous mechanisms and longer prenatal time would be beneficial for the development of myelination.

claim: CM showed a significantly different impact from GA and PT in V1 (p<0.01) and marginal significance in VOTC (p<0.09).

claim: The homotopic connections in all ROIs of ventral cortex were significant (mean r = 0.13–0.43, t > 12.87, p<10–9) in infants scanned within the first day after birth.
source: The homotopic connections in all ROIs of ventral cortex were significant (mean r = 0.13–0.43, t > 12.87, p<10–9; Figure 4a and b) and were significantly higher than adjacent connections (0.29 ± 0.12 vs. 0.19 ± 0.10, Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the Fisher-Z-transformed r-value: z = 16.32, p<10–9) and distal connections (0.04 ± 0.06, z = 16.32, p<10–9; Figure 4c), suggesting that the arealization (homotopic connection) of ventral cortex already existed at birth.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, with reference to figures.
